items.readable_text:
Content:
Given a sphere with radius [MATH: r=4\:\textrm{cm},] how do we calculate its surface area?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0c6d897fee982484b63a7aec75ec89d1]

Content:
We can calculate the surface area [MATH: S] of a sphere using the formula
[MATH: S = 4\pi r^2,]
where [MATH: r] is the radius of the sphere.

Content:
Substituting [MATH: r=4\:\textrm{cm}] into the formula, we obtain
[MATH: S = 4 \pi (4)^2
= 64\pi \:\textrm{cm}^2.]

Content:
We often express the surface area of a sphere as a multiple of [MATH: \pi.] We can also get a numerical approximation using a calculator. In this case, we have

Content:
[MATH: S \approx 201.06 \:\textrm{cm}^2]

Content:
rounded to two decimal places.

items.title: Relating the Surface Area and Volume of a Sphere

sections.normalized_html: The volume of the sphere is [MATH: \dfrac{500}{3}\pi \: \textrm{in}^3.] Calculate the surface area of the sphere.
sections.readable_text: The volume of the sphere is [MATH: \dfrac{500}{3}\pi \: \textrm{in}^3.] Calculate the surface area of the sphere.

sections.normalized_html:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3,]

where [MATH: r] is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting [MATH: V=\dfrac{500}{3}\pi \: \textrm{in}^3] into the formula, we can solve for [MATH: r] as follows:

[MATH: V|= (4)/(3)πr^{3}; (500)/(3)π|= (4)/(3)πr^{3}; (500π ⋅ 3)/(3 ⋅ 4π)|= r^{3}; r^{3}|= 125; r|= 5in]

Finally, the surface area of ​​the sphere is

[MATH: S|= 4πr^{2}; = 4π(5)^{2}; = 100πin^{2}.]
